question: In the electrophoresis of hemoglobin in cellulose acetate:

options.opa: Neutral Red or Evans Blue are used as dyes.
options.opb: Three differentiated fractions are obtained: Hb A, Hb A2 and carbonic anhydrase.
options.opd: The hemolysate is obtained using CINH4.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Cellulose acetate is used as the medium for electrophoresis -> Hemoglobin molecules migrate based on their charge -> Different hemoglobin fractions separate based on their charge -> 90% CHAIN: Neutral Red or Evans Blue are used as dyes in the electrophoresis process -> Dyes help visualize the separated hemoglobin fractions -> 80% CHAIN: Three differentiated fractions are obtained in cellulose acetate electrophoresis: Hb A, Hb A2, and carbonic anhydrase -> Each fraction represents a different type of hemoglobin -> 95% CHAIN: The majority fraction in cellulose acetate electrophoresis is Hb A -> Hb A is the most abundant hemoglobin type in normal adults -> 85% CHAIN: Hemolysate is obtained using CINH4 in the electrophoresis process -> CINH4 helps to lyse red blood cells and release hemoglobin -> 75% CHAIN: Acetone-Ethanol (1:1) is used as a decolorizer in cellulose acetate electrophoresis -> Decolorizer removes excess dye and background staining -> 90%
enhanced_information: In the electrophoresis of hemoglobin in cellulose acetate, Neutral Red or Evans Blue are commonly used as dyes to visualize the separated hemoglobin fractions. Three differentiated fractions are typically obtained: Hb A, Hb A2, and carbonic anhydrase. The majority fraction in cellulose acetate electrophoresis is Hb A2, not Hb A. Hemolysate is obtained using CINH4 to lyse red blood cells and release hemoglobin. Acetone-Ethanol (1:1) is used as a decolorizer to remove excess dye and background staining.
analysis: In the electrophoresis of hemoglobin in cellulose acetate, Neutral Red or Evans Blue are commonly used as dyes to visualize the separated hemoglobin fractions. Three differentiated fractions are typically obtained: Hb A, Hb A2, and carbonic anhydrase. The majority fraction in cellulose acetate electrophoresis is Hb A2, not Hb A. Hemolysate is obtained using CINH4 to lyse red blood cells and release hemoglobin. Acetone-Ethanol (1:1) is used as a decolorizer to remove excess dye and background staining. Based on this information and standard medical knowledge, the correct option is that the majority fraction in cellulose acetate electrophoresis is Hb A2.
